entry.title: October 16, 2026
entry.content:
BigQuery

Feature

Conversational analytics in BigQuery is now available in the following locations:

  • northamerica-northeast1 (Montréal)
  • northamerica-northeast2 (Toronto)

For more information, see Locations.

Dialogflow

Feature

gemini-3.5-flash-lite has become generally available (GA). See Generative quotas for how to request quota for Gemini 3 and later models.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Configure citations for custom MCP data stores

You can configure the citation_mappings parameter for custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) data stores using the REST API to display source citation chips when Gemini Enterprise answers questions using tools on your custom MCP server. This feature is generally available (GA).

For more information, see Configure citations for custom MCP data stores.

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Connect workflows in Workflow Builder to Confluence Data Center and Jira Data Center

You can connect workflows in Workflow Builder to Confluence Data Center and Jira Data Center to search data and automate actions across these third-party apps.

For more information, see Workflows overview.

Google Kubernetes Engine

Change

For GKE Standard CPU node pools, GKE can now upgrade nodes by updating the existing Compute Engine VM in place, instead of deleting the VM and creating a new one. Because the node keeps its underlying VM, it also keeps its compute capacity during the upgrade. This lowers the risk that a node upgrade fails or stalls because resources aren't available.

To enable this type of upgrade, use surge upgrades with the maxUnavailable field set to a value greater than 0. For more details about when GKE reuses the same Compute Engine instance, including exceptions, see maxUnavailable: GKE makes an existing node unavailable to recreate it.

This change applies to all GKE versions. To opt out, contact Cloud Customer Care.

Vertex AI Search

Change

Agent Search: Update to the stable model

The stable model for answer generation is updated to gemini-3.5-flash/answer_gen/v1 from gemini-2.5-flash/answer_gen/v1.

For more information, see Answer generation model versions and lifecycle.

entry.title: October 15, 2026
entry.content:
Apigee Edge for Private Cloud

Announcement

Released Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Designated Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.00 a long-term support (LTS) release: 18 months of full support ending April 2028, then 18 months of maintenance ending October 2029. After October 2029, 4.54.00.00 receives no software updates, security mitigations, or technical support.

Installing a later 4.54 minor release or patch does not change those dates. To extend the support lifecycle, upgrade to the next LTS release.

For the support lifecycle phases, release cadences, and version numbering, see Apigee Edge for Private Cloud release and lifecycle policy.

Announcement

This release replaces Java 8 with Java 17 and Java 21, removes the Classic UI and the apigee-sso component, and updates the bundled Cassandra, Postgres, OpenLDAP, ZooKeeper, Qpid Broker-J, Nginx, and Consul versions. These changes are not backward-compatible.

For the 4.54.00 versions and the 4.53.01 versions they replace, see Supported software and supported versions.

Before upgrading, read Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00, then Update Apigee Edge 4.53.00 or 4.53.01 to 4.54.00 or New installation overview. For known issues, see Known issues with Edge for Private Cloud.

Announcement

Replaced the Classic UI (edge-ui) with the New Edge UI (edge-management-ui).

The New Edge UI is the only management UI in 4.54.00 and is installed by default. Deployments running the Classic UI must transition to it before upgrading. Custom Classic UI properties do not carry over automatically. The default port also changes from 9000 to 3001, configurable with conf_uebe_port, so firewall rules and load balancer target ports that point at 9000 fail until they are updated.

For the migration steps and the supported feature list, see Migrate to the New Edge UI and What features are supported?.

Breaking

In deployments with Apigee SSO enabled, an integrated OIDC identity broker in apigee-openldap replaces the standalone apigee-sso component and Apache Tomcat 9.0.x. Before upgrading, take a complete and validated LDAP backup; existing apigee-sso configurations do not migrate automatically. Deployments not using Apigee SSO require no action.

For migration prerequisites, validation checks, and rollback constraints, see Option 2: Upgrade UI (with Apigee SSO).

Breaking

4.54.00 runs Java in mixed mode: Java 17 for Cassandra and ZooKeeper, Java 21 for the Management Server, Message Processor, Router, and Qpid Broker-J. Both Oracle JDK and OpenJDK are supported at those versions.

Oracle JDK 8 and OpenJDK 8 are no longer supported.

API proxies with custom JavaCallout policies or custom resource JARs can break on Java 21. For details, see Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Change

Upgraded Nginx on the Edge Router to 1.30.0.

If you are upgrading from Nginx 1.20.x, see Nginx 1.30 changes in Apigee Edge 4.54.00 for the full list of changes.

Change

Changed the TLS defaults on Message Processors to the Java 21 cryptographic baseline.

Message Processors run on Java 21, which enables TLS 1.3 by default (JEP 332) and prefers it for outbound backend connections, falling back to TLS 1.2. No configuration change is required if your target servers and load balancers negotiate TLS 1.3, or negotiate TLS 1.2 with forward-secret (ECDHE) cipher suites.

Java 21 also disables the non-forward-secret static RSA key-exchange suites (TLS_RSA_*). If you have overridden conf_http_HTTPTransport.ssl.cipher.suites.whitelist or conf_message-processor-communication_local.http.ssl.ciphers with static RSA suites only, backend calls fail with no cipher suites in common and the Router cannot complete a TLS handshake with the Message Processor. Replace the TLS_RSA_* entries with modern cipher suites and restart the Message Processor.

For the remediation path, see Legacy backend requirements and remediation.

Feature

Added Basic authentication to the New Edge UI, which lets you sign in without configuring an identity provider.

The New Edge UI supports Basic authentication without additional configuration. You can also configure Apigee SSO, or an external identity provider such as SAML or OIDC. This feature is generally available in 4.54.00.

Feature

Added automated pre-flight validation checks to apigee-setup and apigee-service, which surface environment configuration problems before a component is installed.

This feature is generally available in 4.54.00.

Security

Fixed multiple security vulnerabilities in Apigee Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

These fixes ship as part of the component upgrades in this release; see Changes in Edge for Private Cloud 4.54.00.

Change

Changed the default garbage collector on Message Processors to the Garbage-First garbage collector.

Message Processors set useG1GC=true and useStringDeduplication=true by default in 4.54.00. In 4.53.01 neither was set by default. To configure garbage collection, see Configure the garbage collector for Message Processors.

Apigee Edge for Public Cloud

Announcement

On October 15, 2026, we began releasing Single Sign-On (SSO) updates for Apigee Edge for Public Cloud.

Fixed

Bug ID Component Description
560310696 SSO Fixed an issue where the Portal SSO endpoint inadvertently accepted deprecated TLS 1.1 connections. The endpoint now strictly enforces TLS 1.2+.

Apigee Integrated Portal

Announcement

On October 15, 2026, we released a new version of the Apigee integrated portal.

Fixed

Bug ID Description
560310696 Fixed an issue where the Portal SSO endpoint inadvertently accepted deprecated TLS 1.1 connections. The endpoint now strictly enforces TLS 1.2+.

Apigee X

Fixed

Bug ID Description
466116259 Updated the startup script for the managed instance group (MIG) that routes external traffic to Apigee. net.ipv4.ip_forward is now written to /etc/sysctl.d/, so an instance no longer stops forwarding traffic when a reboot or an OS update resets it. The script does not change unrelated iptables NAT rules. Instances pick up the change the next time they are restarted or recreated.

BigQuery

Feature

You can copy tables across regions. This feature is now generally available (GA).

Feature

You can now use column aliases in GoogleSQL. This feature lets you define an alias for an expression in the SELECT clause of a SQL query and immediately reference that alias within the same SELECT list or in the WHERE clause of the same query block.

Column aliases also streamline the migration of workloads from other data warehouses such as Snowflake and Teradata, by supporting their syntax.

This feature is generally available, and is opt-in only. To use column aliases, you must first enable the feature.

Feature

You can export a conversational analytics agent's answer, including text, visualizations, tables, and citations, to a PDF or CSV file. This feature is generally available (GA).

Cloud Vision

Deprecated

Face detection model update

The emotion label response in the Cloud Vision API is deprecated. Going forward, the Cloud Vision API face detection (FACE_DETECTION feature) will return UNKNOWN for all emotion-related labels.

Compute Engine

Feature

Preview: You can create regional disks, including Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability volumes, by cloning a zonal boot disk.

For more information, see Duplicate a disk with clones.

Change

If you try to create an on-demand reservation or increase the number of reserved Compute Engine instances in a reservation when the zone has reached its reservation capacity limit for your requested machine family, then the request fails with a RESERVATION_CAPACITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED error. For more information, see Reservation capacity limit exceeded.

Feature

Generally available: The storage-optimized Z4M machine series is generally available for Compute Engine. Powered by fifth generation Intel Emerald Rapids Xeon Scalable processors and Titanium offload processors, Z4M instances are purpose-built for workloads that require larger storage capacity, such as:

  • Parallel file systems to support AI/ML workloads
  • I/O intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and vector databases
  • AI/ML training and inference workloads such as checkpointing and distributed Key-Value (KV) cache

The Z4M machine series delivers up to 1,536 GB of memory and 168,000 GiB of local Titanium SSD capacity. Z4M also supports up to 400 Gbps of network bandwidth using two physical NICs. Z4M instances use Titanium and Cloud RDMA to help enable higher levels of networking performance, isolation, and security.

For more information, see Storage-optimized machine family.

Dataflow

Feature

Dataflow Auto VM Selection now supports 4th generation Compute Engine machine series. When Auto VM Selection is enabled, the service prioritizes these newer generation VMs for improved performance. If 4th generation VMs are unavailable at startup, the service automatically falls back to widely available 2nd generation machine families to ensure that your jobs can start without unnecessary delays.

For more information, see Auto VM Selection.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Anthropic models are available in the Gemini Enterprise app

Administrators can make Anthropic models—Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5—available to users in the Gemini Enterprise app. After an administrator turns on a model in the Enable third-party models section of the Feature Management tab, users can select the model in the model selector. Claude models are available in the global location and the us and eu multi-regions, and are charged on a pay-as-you-go basis.

This feature is generally available. For more information, see Enable third-party models.

Looker

Feature

The Looker 26.18 features have begun to be enabled for Looker (Google Cloud core) instances.

NetApp Volumes

Announcement

Google Cloud NetApp Volumes now supports the Flex Unified service level, including custom performance, in the following region:

  • europe-west8 (Milan)

For more information about available regions, see Supported regions.

Security Command Center

Feature

To increase the precision of attack path analysis and provide attack exposure scores that help you prioritize confirmed internet exposures, Risk Engine attack path simulations support the EXTERNALLY_EXPOSED_VM_INSTANCE External Exposure finding category (Preview). This finding category identifies Compute Engine or Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) resources with a direct public IP address that allows host OS access.

For more information, see Detect exposed resources, Risk Engine feature support, and Overview of attack exposure scores and attack paths.

Video Intelligence API

Deprecated

We are deprecating the emotion label response in the API. Going forward, the API will return UNKNOWN for all emotion related labels.

entry.title: October 14, 2026
entry.content:
Anti Money Laundering AI

Announcement

New minor engine version released for the commercial line of business within the v004.011 version line (aml-commercial.default.v004.011.202610-000). This version extends support for the major engine version and includes no significant changes compared to the previous minor version.

Apigee hybrid

Announcement

v1.16.11

On October 14, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.16.11.

  • For information on upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to version v1.16.11.
  • For information on new installations, see The big picture.
Note: This is a patch release: The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch via the Helm chart automatically updates the images. No manual image changes are typically needed. For information on container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Fixed

Fixed in this release

Bug ID Description
565072374 Fixed an issue where VerifyJWT policies using a JWKS uriRef could return steps.jwt.NoMatchingPublicKey on the first request after the 5-minute JWKS cache TTL expired when the identity provider rotated keys. The cache now refreshes synchronously upon expiration.
556680325 Fixed a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in URL host validation for the SemanticCacheLookup policy.
535395491 Extension Processor (ext_proc) denials now return the status and body that the policy or FaultRule produced, instead of always returning HTTP 500.
513032450 Fixed an issue where apigee-connect-agent control-plane connections could hang for up to 2 hours when silently dropped by a network intermediary by restoring a 15-second TCP keep-alive.
502540992 Fixed an issue where the SemanticCacheLookup policy was incompatible with Vertex AI Vector Search Private Service Connect (PSC) endpoints by adding gRPC transport support via <PrivateServiceConnect><GrpcEndpoint>.
492042425 Fixed an issue in the LLMTokenQuota policy where operation-level token quota values configured on an API product were not applied at runtime, causing product-level quota values to be enforced instead.

Application Integration

Security

An Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the AuthConfig validation and integration execution runtime in Application Integration versions prior to August 27, 2026. For more information, see the GCP-2026-068 security bulletin.

BigQuery

Feature

The Apache Hive catalog endpoint in the Lakehouse runtime catalog is now generally available (GA). This integration lets you use the metastore as a serverless, central metadata layer, enabling seamless data sharing and unified querying across Apache Spark, Apache Hive, and BigQuery.

For more information, see About the Hive catalog endpoint and Set up Spark and Hive with the Lakehouse runtime catalog.

Feature

Metadata migration from Dataproc Metastore to Lakehouse is now generally available (GA). You can perform a one-time backfill migration or dry run to migrate metadata from a Dataproc Metastore service to an Apache Iceberg REST catalog endpoint or a Hive catalog endpoint using the Google Cloud console, the gcloud CLI, or the REST API.

For more information, see Migrate metadata from Dataproc Metastore to Lakehouse.

Feature

Conversational analytics now lets you create a conversation with all of the data sources in multiple projects, or create a conversation with a dataset. These features are generally available (GA).

Feature

You can publish a BigQuery Conversational Analytics agent in Gemini Enterprise. This feature is now generally available (GA).

Feature

The AI.AGG function now supports the output_schema argument, which lets you specify the schema of the function output as a comma-separated list of fields. This feature is generally available (GA).

Certificate Manager

Change

Google-managed public SSL certificates signed by Google Public CA (pki.goog) are gradually transitioning from a 90-day validity period to a 45-day validity period to improve security.

To align with modern industry-wide security standards and promote shorter certificate lifespans, Google-managed public certificates now rotate more frequently. This proactive rotation enhances the overall security posture of load balancers. The transition requires no manual intervention or configuration changes as Certificate Manager automatically manages both issuance and renewal.

For more information, see Google-managed certificates and Use Google-managed certificates.

Cloud Load Balancing

Change

Google-managed public SSL certificates signed by Public Certificate Authority (pki.goog) are gradually transitioning from a 90-day validity period to a 45-day validity period to improve security.

To align with modern industry-wide security standards and promote shorter certificate lifespans, Google-managed public certificates signed by Public Certificate Authority now rotate more frequently.

This proactive rotation enhances the overall security posture of load balancers. Transition requires no manual intervention or configuration changes as Google Cloud automatically manages issuance and renewal for both Certificate Manager and Compute Engine SSL certificates.

For more information, see Renew a Google-managed SSL certificate.

Feature

Service rate limiting policies are now available in Preview for regional internal Application Load Balancers and Secure Web Proxies.

Service rate limiting policies let you maintain service availability among trusted clients that might consume an inordinate amount of resources.

For more information, see the Service rate limiting overview.

Cloud SQL for MySQL

Issue

When you enable the Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog) integration on a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance created before April 18, 2026, the integration defaults to once a day instead of near real-time.

Near real-time updates upon Knowledge Catalog enablement aren't yet available for all existing instances. A new announcement will be published when this feature becomes available.

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

Issue

When you enable the Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog) integration on a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance created before April 18, 2026, the integration defaults to once a day instead of near real-time.

Near real-time updates upon Knowledge Catalog enablement aren't yet available for all existing instances. A new announcement will be published when this feature becomes available.

Compute Engine

Feature

Generally available: When you reserve capacity by using future reservation requests, you can specify that Compute Engine delivers your reserved capacity as specifically targeted reservations. Specifically targeted reservations help you track and control which Compute Engine instances consume your reserved capacity. For more information, see About future reservation requests.

Feature

Generally available: You can increase the size of a Google Cloud Hyperdisk volume that's in multi-writer mode while the volume is attached to multiple instances. Previously, you had to detach the volume from all instances before you could resize it.

For more information, see Share disks between instances and Change the size or provisioned performance of a Hyperdisk volume.

Dataform

Feature

You can automatically preserve BigQuery data policies and data governance tags (Preview) applied to tables across Dataform executions by enabling the preserveGovernanceControls option in your table or workflow configuration. For more information, see Preserve access controls metadata. This feature is generally available (GA).

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 3.8 Flash regional availability in the United Kingdom

Gemini 3.8 Flash is generally available (GA) in the United Kingdom.

  • Location availability: Supported in the UK (europe-west2) in-country region with in-region at-rest data residency (DRZ) and machine learning processing (MLP).
  • App availability: Turned on by default in the web app for the UK region. Administrators can manage access with the Gemini 3.8 Flash toggle under Model availability.

For more information, see Data residency for Gemini Enterprise.

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Argon available in Workflow Builder

Gemini 4 Argon is generally available (GA) for Workflow Builder. Gemini 4 Argon is also available in Workflow Builder workflow agents. Updates take up to a day to appear in workflow agents.

  • Location availability: Supported in global, us, and eu multi-regions, with data residency and ML processing support in us and eu. For more information, see Data residency for Gemini Enterprise.
  • App availability: Turned off by default. The toggle defaults to on beginning October 27, 2026. For instructions to turn on the model, see Manage features on the web app.

For more information, see Workflow Builder.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Priority PayGo support for Gemini Nano Banana 2.1

Priority Pay-as-you-go (PayGo) is available in General Availability (GA) for Gemini Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1) on the global endpoint.

Fixed

CodeMender updates (v0.15.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Enhanced SARIF 2.1.0 reporting: Updated cm report SARIF output with standardized rule descriptors, severity properties, and repository-relative artifact locations for improved GitHub Code Scanning compatibility.
  • Model invocation metrics: Added model invocation tracking to cm stats --json, providing total, per-session, and per-turn invocation counts.
  • Bug fixes:
    • Fixed an issue where token usage from completed turns was omitted from session logs during error or cancellation exit paths.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

Feature

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is available in Public Preview

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash from DeepSeek is available as a fully managed model (MaaS) in Model Garden. The model accepts text and image input, targets agentic and coding tasks, and supports a context window of up to 1M tokens.

For more information, see DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

Google Cloud Armor

Feature

Cloud Armor supports service rate limiting. For more information, see Cloud Armor and service rate limiting. This feature is available in Preview.

Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka

Feature

Performance of the Cloud Storage Sink connector has been improved. The improvements include reduced out-of-memory errors, higher maximum throughput, and avoiding creating a large number of small files.

Google Kubernetes Engine

Change

(2026-R44) Version updates

GKE cluster versions have been updated.

New versions available for upgrades and new clusters.

The following versions are now available for new GKE clusters, and for manual control plane upgrades and node upgrades for existing clusters. For more information about versioning and upgrades, see GKE versioning and support and About GKE cluster upgrades.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow

Announcement

All Managed Airflow environment's GKE clusters will be set up with maintenance exclusions from November 16, 2026 to December 2, 2026. For more information, see Maintenance exclusions.

NetApp Volumes

Feature

Google Cloud NetApp Volumes now lets you test Active Directory policy connections for the Flex Unified service level in Preview. You can use the Google Cloud console to verify that a policy is properly connected to the Active Directory service and troubleshoot configuration errors. For more information, see Test the Active Directory policy connection.

Secure Web Proxy

Feature

Secure Web Proxy supports service rate limiting policies. Use these policies to protect external destinations from traffic overloads and manage the costs of your outbound web traffic.

You can attach a service rate limiting policy to your Secure Web Proxy gateways, whether they use an authorization policy or a gateway security policy. For more information, see Configure service rate limiting policies.

This feature is available in Preview.

VPC Service Controls

Feature

VPC Service Controls feature (Status: Preview): Support for using Workload Identity Federation for GKE in ingress and egress rules to allow access to resources protected by a service perimeter is available in Preview.

You can specify the following Workload Identity Federation for GKE principals in ingress and egress rules:

  • All GKE Pods that use a Kubernetes service account (by service account name or ID)
  • All GKE Pods in a Kubernetes namespace
  • All GKE Pods in a cluster

For more information, see Configure identity groups and third-party identities in ingress and egress rules and Supported identities for ingress and egress rules.

entry.title: October 13, 2026
entry.content:
BigQuery

Feature

The AI.AGG function is generally available (GA). You can use this function to semantically aggregate unstructured input data based on natural language instructions.

Feature

BigQuery generative AI functions now support the gemini-4-argon model. This model is generally available.

Cloud Asset Inventory

Feature

The following resource types are publicly available through the ExportAssets, ListAssets, BatchGetAssetsHistory, QueryAssets, Feed, and Search (SearchAllResources, SearchAllIamPolicies) APIs.

  • Cloud Service Mesh: networkservices.googleapis.com/AgentGateway

Cloud Billing

Feature

Spend cap budgets are now generally available for a limited set of services

For eligible services, you can configure a spend cap budget to automatically pause usage when your estimated spend exceeds the budget amount you set. You can manage spend cap budgets in the Budgets page in the Google Cloud console and using the Cloud Billing Budget API.

Spend caps are a cost control mechanism. A spend cap is enforced when usage costs exceed your budget target amount. When enforced, any new request to the eligible services, within the specified project, are paused and no further usage costs are accrued until the spend cap is lifted. You can manually lift an enforced spend cap, or wait until the start of the next month when the spend cap is automatically lifted.

Spend caps use gross, estimated costs to trigger the alerts and caps, enforcing a cap much faster than the actual costs are processed and appear on billing reports. Even though faster than reports, the enforcement of spend caps isn't instant and any cost overages are billed as normal.

More information about spend cap budgets

For managing spend cap budgets in the Google Cloud console, see:

  • How spend cap budgets work to help you control spend
  • Limitations of spend cap budgets
  • Configure a spend cap budget
  • Lift an enforced spend cap

For managing spend cap budgets using the Cloud Billing Budget API, see:

  • Using the Cloud Billing Budget API for spend cap budgets
  • Spend cap budget concepts and limitations
  • Create a spend cap budget
  • Lift an enforced spend cap
  • Cloud Billing Budget API REST reference

Cloud SQL for MySQL

Feature

Private Service Connect is now the default private IP connectivity option when you create a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance in a new Google Cloud project. Private Service Connect lets you connect to your instance from multiple Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks across different groups, projects, or organizations, and supports automatic endpoint and DNS record provisioning. When you configure private IP for an instance, you can still choose to use private services access or both connectivity options.

For more information, see Private IP configuration options and Configure Private Service Connect.

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

Feature

Private Service Connect is now the default private IP connectivity option when you create a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance in a new Google Cloud project. Private Service Connect lets you connect to your instance from multiple Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks across different groups, projects, or organizations, and supports automatic endpoint and DNS record provisioning. When you configure private IP for an instance, you can still choose to use private services access or both connectivity options.

For more information, see Private IP configuration options and Configure Private Service Connect.

Cloud SQL for SQL Server

Feature

Private Service Connect is now the default private IP connectivity option when you create a Cloud SQL for SQL Server instance in a new Google Cloud project. Private Service Connect lets you connect to your instance from multiple Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks across different groups, projects, or organizations, and supports automatic endpoint and DNS record provisioning. When you configure private IP for an instance, you can still choose to use private services access or both connectivity options.

For more information, see Private IP configuration options and Configure Private Service Connect.

Cloud Storage

Feature

Object enrichments is now available in Preview. When you configure object enrichments, Cloud Storage applies Google's pre-trained machine learning models to eligible images and PDF documents in your buckets and attaches the resulting metadata to your objects as object contexts. You can inspect enrichments on individual objects or query them at scale in BigQuery by using Storage Insights datasets. For more information, see About object enrichments and Configure object enrichments.

Feature

Object contexts with extended data are available in Preview. Google services attach these contexts to your objects during automated analysis, such as machine learning labeling. To retrieve a context and its extended data, use the viewFullContext JSON API method.

Feature

Storage Insights datasets include the Object Contexts Catalog view (object_contexts_catalog_view), which you can use to analyze object contexts in BigQuery. For more information, see Object contexts catalog and Analyze object contexts.

Cluster Toolkit

Feature

Cluster Toolkit v1.106.0 is available. This release adds support for flexible managed instance groups on static compute nodes, multiple network interfaces (multi-NIC) for Google Cloud Managed Lustre instances, and parallelism controls for Terraform to accelerate cluster deployment and teardown.

This release also introduces the cloud-build community module to build container images with Cloud Build.

Additionally, this release adds preflight checks for storage profiles when you submit jobs and cleans up gateways when you cancel jobs.

This update also scopes the --main-only flag in the gcluster job logs command to the main Pod and its default container.

For more information, see the release announcement on GitHub.

Compute Engine

Feature

Generally available: You can query regional views of global Compute Engine project and OS image resources by using the regional read-only projectViews and imageViews endpoints. Querying regional views isolates your control-plane read requests to a specific region, helping your workloads stay available during global API disruptions. For more information, see Use regional views for resilient control-plane reads and Access global resources regionally for high availability.

Config Connector

Announcement

Config Connector version 1.159.0 is now available.

Feature

New Alpha Resources (Direct Reconciler):

  • AIPlatformReasoningEngine

    • Manage Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform reasoning engines to deploy and run customized reasoning applications.

  • CloudDeployCustomTargetType

    • Manage Cloud Deploy custom target types to define custom deployment targets and rendering actions.

  • EventarcPipeline

    • Manage Eventarc pipelines to transform and route events across Google Cloud services.

  • LiveStreamChannel

    • Manage Live Stream channels to ingest, encode, and distribute live video streams.

  • LiveStreamInput

    • Manage Live Stream inputs to configure video ingestion endpoints.

  • MapManagementStyleConfig

    • Manage Map Management API style configurations to define custom map styles.

  • NetworkSecurityDNSThreatDetector

    • Manage Network Security DNS threat detectors to monitor and mitigate DNS-based threats.

Feature

New Fields:

  • ArtifactRegistryRepository

    • Added support for spec.remoteRepositoryConfig.commonRepository.

  • ComposerEnvironment

    • Added support for updating spec.config.workloadsConfig.dagProcessor in Cloud Composer 3 environments.

  • ContainerCluster

    • Added support for spec.privilegedAdmissionConfig to configure privileged admission in Autopilot clusters.

  • SQLInstance

    • Added support for disaster recovery observed state fields under status.observedState.replicationCluster (failoverDRReplicaName, drReplica, psaWriteEndpoint) and status.observedState.masterInstanceName.

Feature

New Features:

  • Added support for Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition disaster recovery (DR) pair setup and drift suppression for SQLInstance by using the cnrm.cloud.google.com/sqlinstance-advanced-dr: "enabled" annotation.
  • Manager Pods now restart automatically when resourceSettings changes in the operator configuration.
  • Added a guide for managing Config Connector by using GitOps tools (such as Argo CD).

Fixed

Bug Fixes:

  • BigQueryDataset (#13352)

    • Fixed false-positive diffs for access entries and avoided redundant PATCH requests when the resource is already up to date.

  • ComputeRouterNAT (#13472)

    • Fixed false drift and steady-state reconciliation issues during direct controller takeover.

  • MonitoringDashboard (#13574)

    • Fixed reconciliation errors caused by unrecognized enum values by migrating the direct controller to the Google REST client.

Dataform

Feature

You can use Developer Connect to connect Dataform repositories to Secure Source Manager repositories. This feature is in Preview.

Gemini Enterprise

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Argon available in web app, mobile app, and AI developer tools

Gemini 4 Argon is generally available (GA) for the Gemini Enterprise web app, mobile app, and AI developer tools.

  • Location availability: Supported in global, us, and eu multi-regions, with data residency and ML processing support in us and eu. For more information, see Data residency for Gemini Enterprise.
  • App availability: Turned off by default. The toggle defaults to on beginning October 27, 2026. Gemini 4 Argon is supported in the web app and mobile app. For more information about turning on the model, see Manage features on the web app.
  • AI developer tools: Enabled by default for licensed users when Antigravity authorized models uses the default selection. If your organization specifies a custom model list, an administrator must manually select Gemini 4 Argon. For more information, see Configure AI developer tools settings.

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Connect workflows in Workflow Builder to Microsoft Teams, Notion, and Salesforce

You can connect workflows in Workflow Builder to Microsoft Teams, Notion, and Salesforce to search data and automate actions across these third-party apps.

For more information, see Workflows overview.

Feature

Gemini Enterprise: Gemini 4 Argon is available in AlphaEvolve

AlphaEvolve experiments can generate candidate programs with Gemini 4 Argon in the global, us, and eu regions. To use it, specify gemini-4-argon in the models field of generationSettings. Gemini 3.8 Flash remains the default model.

For more information, see Supported models and AlphaEvolve limitations.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

Feature

Gemini 4 Argon in CodeMender (Preview)

CodeMender now supports Gemini 4 Argon. To use it, pass --model gemini-4-argon to cm find, cm verify, or cm fix. Gemini 3.8 Flash remains the default model.

For more information, see Specifying the model.

Feature

Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Argon Cyber Permissive

Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon) is available in General Availability (GA). Gemini 4 Argon is Google's frontier model that excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. It supports a unified 1,048,576-token input and output limit, configurable thinking levels (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH), long decodes up to 1,048,576 tokens using continuation tokens on the GenerateContent API, and agentic video understanding in GA.

Gemini 4 Argon Cyber Permissive (gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive), a version of Gemini 4 Argon for defensive cybersecurity use cases, is also available in GA behind the Fairwind Program allowlist.

  • Known issue (long decodes): Long decoding (continuation_token) on the GenerateContent API (generateContent and streamGenerateContent) is supported only in the v1beta1 API (not v1). The Google Gen AI SDK uses v1beta1 by default unless api_version='v1' is specified in http_options; for direct REST calls, use the v1beta1 endpoint path.

For more information, see Get started with Gemini 4 and the developer's guide to Gemini 4 Argon.

Google Cloud Contact Center as a Service

Announcement

Google Cloud CCaaS prerelease notes 6.22

Here are the pre-release notes for what we expect to be the next version of Google Cloud CCaaS. When we release this version, we expect the new capabilities to be as shown here.

Feature

Campaign-based scheduled callbacks

Agents can now schedule a callback during an outbound campaign call. The callback belongs to the campaign, not to an individual agent, and the dialer calls the consumer back in the time slot they chose. Administrators set slot length, capacity, booking window, and expiry for each campaign, and supervisors can track upcoming, completed, and expired callbacks from the campaign list.

Feature

Transcript separation for chat

You can now configure Google Cloud CCaaS to deliver a separate transcript file for each participant segment in a chat, instead of one combined transcript per session. Under Settings > Chat > Chat Transcript, select Per Segment in Transcript Separation to generate individual transcript files for each agent, virtual agent, or supervisor who joins the chat—helpful for identifying which participant handled each part of a transferred or escalated conversation. Your consumers still receive a single, full-chat transcript regardless of this setting.

By default, this capability is inactive. Contact Google Cloud Support to turn it on for your instance.

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  • Fixed an issue where direct access point (DAP) greeting messages played twice when a call was deflected to an internal phone number due to queue overcapacity.

  • Fixed an issue where session metadata for top-level menu paths and selected menus was incorrectly displayed in English instead of the user's configured language.

  • Fixed an issue where a failed Salesforce lookup was incorrectly treated as having no matches, which resulted in the creation of duplicate records.

  • Fixed an issue where inbound transfer restrictions remained in force even after being hidden in the administrator interface, causing queues to become silently unreachable for transfers.

  • Fixed an issue where hold music continued to play throughout a call recording after a warm transfer was completed.

  • Fixed an issue where outbound virtual agent audio was prematurely truncated during multi-message turns.

  • Fixed an issue where the Real-time Monitoring Queues report didn't accurately count skill-matched agents for skills-based queues, often displaying zero available agents despite their availability.

  • Fixed an issue where calls deflected to an external phone number after entering a queue were incorrectly recorded as abandoned by the customer.

  • Fixed an issue where the credit card tokenizer was missing from the SmartActions menu during outbound callback calls.

  • Fixed an issue where mandatory call dispositions were discarded if an agent's voice connection dropped but their session remained active.

  • Fixed an issue where the text resize menu in the chat widget wasn't scrollable at 400% browser zoom, which prevented users from accessing all available text size options.

  • Fixed an issue where the system incorrectly prevented saving automatic call redirection settings when the target was a virtual agent-operated queue.

  • Fixed an issue where duplicate call records were created for a single inbound call, causing incorrect wait times to appear in the real-time queue view.

  • Fixed an issue where empty data attributes caused an error in the agent interface during call connections.

  • Fixed an issue where the Transfer Restrictions destination picker provided no feedback when a queue was ineligible, making it indistinguishable from a typo or search error.

  • Fixed an issue where incoming calls were rejected with a SIP 603 error due to high database latency and connection timeouts.

  • Fixed an issue where the documentation for the Apps API and call session metadata schema didn't define the top-level parentId and finishReason fields.

  • Fixed an issue where certain inbound call failures were incorrectly reported as a busy signal.

  • Fixed an issue where the event processor service crashed during scaling or rebalancing of the system.

  • Fixed an issue where the conversation ID was missing from chat events during active sessions.

  • Fixed an issue where report exports didn't download or remained stuck in a processing state indefinitely.

  • Fixed an issue where agents could transfer calls to queues that were already closed if their transfer list was loaded while the queue was still open.

  • Fixed an issue where queued chats were assigned to agents after the end-user had become unresponsive without being prompted to check in.

  • Fixed an issue where voice calls cold-transferred to an over-capacity queue generated duplicate reporting records and incorrect queue wait times if the callback leg failed.

  • Fixed an issue where direct inbound calls deflected to voicemail during after-hours played three separate audio prompts sequentially.

  • Fixed an issue where a single call was simultaneously assigned to two different agents if the pickup coincided with the cascade timer expiry.

  • Fixed an issue where direct inbound calls weren't projected to agents in a breakthrough-enabled status if another call was already waiting in their queue.

  • Fixed an issue where a gray empty area appeared below the chat container in the agent adapter when the iframe width was narrower than 449px.

  • Fixed an issue where several Kubernetes and Google Cloud service accounts were granted overly broad permissions, which could have allowed for unauthorized privilege escalation.

  • Fixed an issue where an agent's status sequence was recorded in the incorrect order following a brief connection loss during an active chat.

  • Fixed an issue where selecting a contact during a native campaign call didn't automatically open the corresponding record in the CRM.

  • Fixed an issue where AI-generated Smart Disposition suggestions were inconsistently displayed for outbound calls during the wrap-up period.

  • Fixed an issue where call recordings became distorted or garbled when multiple holds were placed during a call.

  • Fixed an issue where audio uploads were accepted based on the file extension rather than the actual file content, which caused call disconnections when incompatible formats were played.

  • Fixed an issue where the call duration timer in the external call adapter didn't match the In-call status timer in the agent desktop for inbound calls.

  • Fixed an issue where the sentiment score was incorrectly displayed in the call adapter for calls escalated from a virtual agent, even when the Sentiment Analysis setting was disabled.

  • Fixed an issue where duplicate reporting rows were generated for call and wrap-up durations due to concurrent system events.

  • Fixed an issue where agents couldn't sign in or refresh their status if their account was linked to a deleted or unknown status.

  • Fixed an issue where the Manager API documentation for agent activity logs omitted 17 chat routing and activity values, leading to incomplete reporting data for customers.

  • Fixed an issue where IVR custom callback numbers for certain international regions, including Norway and Denmark, were incorrectly dialed with a +1 prefix.

  • Fixed an issue where metadata for calls deflected between virtual agent assignment and connection wasn't exported to the Cloud Storage bucket.

  • Fixed an issue where virtual agent to human chat escalations experienced delays of up to 300 seconds during agent assignment.

  • Fixed an issue where the Answer button didn't appear for dial-by-extension calls when other calls were already waiting in an agent's queue.

  • Fixed an issue where a supervisor's name didn't appear in the chat widget when joining a conversation using the monitor then barge workflow.

  • Fixed an issue where ending a chat session in one browser tab didn't automatically close the chat widget in other open tabs.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow

Announcement

A new Managed Service for Apache Airflow release has started on October 13, 2026. Get ready for upcoming changes and features as we roll out the new release to all regions. This release is in progress at the moment. Listed changes and features might not be available in some regions yet.

Feature

Development mode environments and Environment hibernation are now generally available (GA).

You can now create Managed Airflow (Gen 3) environments with Airflow 3 in development mode to test and develop DAGs before publishing them to production. You can hibernate development mode environments when you no longer need them. Hibernation reduces most environment costs to zero.

Feature

Upgrade rollbacks are available in Managed Airflow (Gen 3). You can roll back an environment upgrade if you encounter degraded performance, Airflow bugs, or compatibility issues with your DAGs, plugins, or dependencies.

This feature is gradually rolling out over several releases. In this release, it's available in the following regions: europe-north1, europe-west3, us-east1, and us-west2.

Feature

New Managed Airflow (Gen 3) environments created while the Restrict Endpoint Usage (constraints/gcp.restrictEndpointUsage) organization policy is active now use regional endpoints for services like Cloud Storage, Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, and Data Lineage.

Feature

(Managed Airflow Gen 3) Added the scheduler loop duration metric:

  • composer.googleapis.com/workload/scheduler/loop_duration: time spent running one Scheduler loop.

Feature

Database retention in Managed Airflow (Gen 3) now includes new Airflow 3 metadata tables, and updated retention logs to report the exact number of removed rows.

This feature is gradually rolling out over several releases. In this release, it's available in the following regions: europe-north1, europe-west3, us-east1, and us-west2.

Fixed

Managed Airflow (Gen 3) environments now report Airflow workloads startup failure logs for issues such as internal quota limits, insufficient capacity, or internal errors (excluding failures related to KubernetesPodOperator or KubernetesExecutor).

This fix is available without an upgrade and will gradually roll out to all Managed Airflow Gen 3 environments. You can upgrade your environment to receive this update immediately.

Fixed

Fixed an issue where a redundant image-version property set in the API request body could sometimes cause a long-running operation to fail.

Fixed

(Managed Airflow Gen 2) Fixed an issue where the airflow-monitoring pod could run out of memory (OOMKilled) when calculating scheduled snapshot metrics in environments with a large number of files in their environment's bucket.

Change

The apache-airflow-providers-google package was upgraded to version 22.6.0. For more information about changes, see the apache-airflow-providers-google changelog.

Deprecated

The following Managed Airflow versions and builds have reached their end of support period: composer-3-airflow-2.9.3-build.35, composer-3-airflow-2.10.5-build.15, composer-3-airflow-2.9.3-build.36, composer-3-airflow-2.10.5-build.16, composer-2.14.3-airflow-2.9.3, composer-2.14.3-airflow-2.10.5, composer-2.14.4-airflow-2.9.3, and composer-2.14.4-airflow-2.10.5.

Change

The apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes package was upgraded to version 10.23.0. For changes in other packages, see the preinstalled packages changelog.

Change

New images are available in Managed Airflow (Gen 2):

  • composer-2.17.15-airflow-2.11.1 (default)

Change

New Airflow builds are available in Managed Airflow (Gen 3):

  • composer-3-airflow-3.3.1-build.4
  • composer-3-airflow-3.2.2-build.8
  • composer-3-airflow-2.11.1-build.21 (default)

Cloud Build

You can now choose the release channel for your build config or private pool. The release channel determines how frequently the underlying versions of Debian and Docker are updated.

Cloud DNS

Feature

Attach Outbound Endpoints to forwarding zones or server policies to enable direct DNS query forwarding from VPC networks to external and on-premises DNS resolvers using private IP addresses. For more information, see Outbound Endpoints overview.

Cloud Load Balancing

Feature

Regular expression matchers in host and route rules in URL maps are now generally available (GA).

You can now use regular expressions (regex) matchers to configure more flexible and precise traffic routing rules within URL maps for Application Load Balancers. This feature allows you to leverage the power of RE2 syntax for matching on:

  • URL Paths: Using the regexMatch field within routeRules.
  • HTTP Headers: Using the regexMatch field within headerMatches in routeRules.
  • HTTP Query Parameters: Using the regexMatch field within queryParameterMatches in routeRules.

This feature is available in:

  • Global external Application Load Balancers
  • Regional internal Application Load Balancers
  • Cross-region internal Application Load Balancers
  • Regional external Application Load Balancers

For more information, see URL map concepts: Regular expressions matchers in host and route rules.

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

CodeMender updates (v0.14.0)

This release introduces updates to CodeMender:

  • Better pull request scans: cm find --diff now catches removed security controls and gives large files more time (configurable with --diff-job-timeout).
  • Unified sessions: --deep and --diff scans now appear as a single session in cm session list, cm report, and cm stats.
  • Moved code in cm verify: cm verify now finds code that moved since cm find and updates the finding's location.
  • Guided activation: cm now opens the activation page and waits for activation instead of exiting.
  • New cm find flags: --deep-max-turns limits exploratory steps per file in --deep scans, and --enable-bash allows shell commands during scans.
  • Improved detection: More distinct findings per file and more precise CWE classification for weak hashing and randomness.
  • Bug fixes:
    • Fixed scans of repositories reached through nested symbolic links.
    • Fixed findings for nonexistent files and over-merged findings.
    • Shell scripts created by cm verify are now executable.

For more information, see the CodeMender documentation.

Announcement

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for VMware

Announcement

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for VMware 1.35.600-gke.140 is now available for download. To upgrade, see Upgrade clusters. Google Distributed Cloud 1.35.600-gke.140 runs on Kubernetes v1.35.8-gke.100.

If you use a third-party storage vendor, check the listing of our previously-qualified storage partners.

After a release, it takes approximately 7 to 14 days for the version to become available for use with GKE On-Prem API clients: the Google Cloud console, the gcloud CLI, and Terraform.

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.35.600-gke.140:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.
  • Fixed an issue where user clusters repeatedly alternated between reconciling and running states if the management cluster configured a different pod density configuration than the user cluster.

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal

Announcement

Google Distributed Cloud (software only) for bare metal 1.35.600-gke.140 is now available for download. To upgrade, see Upgrade clusters. Google Distributed Cloud for bare metal 1.35.600-gke.140 runs on Kubernetes v1.35.8-gke.100.

After a release, it takes approximately 7 to 14 days for the version to become available for installations or upgrades with the GKE On-Prem API clients: the Google Cloud console, the gcloud CLI, and Terraform.

If you use a third-party storage vendor, check the listing of our previously-qualified storage partners.

Fixed

The following issues were fixed in 1.35.600-gke.140:

  • Fixed vulnerabilities listed in Vulnerability fixes.
  • Improved containerd resilience against state corruption if a node reboots while unpacking container images.
  • Fixed an issue where the periodic configuration drift health check failed with a version not supported error while a cluster upgrade or rollback was in progress.
  • Fixed an issue where audit-proxy retried audit log exports indefinitely on permanent errors, generating excessive audit logging traffic.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kubernetes preflight health check scanned all namespaces in the admin cluster instead of the target cluster's namespace, causing cluster upgrades to fail if an unrelated cluster had stale reconciling resources.
  • Fixed an issue where upgrading or recreating a node during maintenance mode could proceed before storage volumes finished detaching, resulting in orphaned CSI VolumeAttachment resources or I/O errors. After the fix, node drain verifies that kubelet unmounts all host volumes and that CSI VolumeAttachment resources detach before completing the drain.
  • Fixed an issue where Certificate Authority (CA) rotation failed for self-managing clusters (admin, hybrid, and standalone). The failure occurs during the final phase of the rotation when attempting to move management resources back from the temporary bootstrap cluster to the self-managing cluster, which can leave the cluster in an unmanageable state. You must upgrade your clusters to version 1.35.600-gke.140 before you rotate your CAs.
  • Fixed an issue where BareMetalMachine status conditions prematurely reported nodes as ready and available during maintenance mode transitions.
  • Fixed an issue in clusters using bundled BGP load balancing where control plane upgrades or configuration updates could cause up to 20 seconds of API server connection failures while a control plane node restarted. After the fix, failover to a healthy control plane node completes in approximately 4 seconds.
  • Fixed an issue where user clusters repeatedly alternated between reconciling and running states if the management cluster configured a different pod density configuration than the user cluster.

Google SecOps

Feature

Applied Threat Intelligence curated rules now use the GTI_IOC feed

As a follow-up to the release of the GTI_IOC feed and the deprecation of the legacy MANDIANT_ACTIVE_BREACH_IOC, MANDIANT_FUSION_IOC, and OPEN_SOURCE_INTEL_IOC feeds, the Applied Threat Intelligence (ATI) curated detection rules are being updated to match against the GTI_IOC feed. You don't need to take any action for curated rules. Updated rules continue to match only on reviewed, stable indicators. If you have custom rules that still reference the legacy feeds, update them to use the GTI_IOC feed. For more information, see Migrate to GTI_IOC.

The update follows the standard Google SecOps rollout schedule. It starts on Monday, October 12, 2026 and rolls out to all regions during the week.

Feature

[Spotlight Feature] Monitor response and playbook health with the Response Health Hub

Google SecOps now includes the Response Health Hub curated dashboard, a central location for monitoring playbook performance, execution latency, automation effectiveness, and integration health across environments.

Key capabilities include:

  • Volume and adoption tracking: Monitor total playbook execution volume, daily trends, completion success rates, and queued playbook backlogs.
  • Attachment and rerun insights: Track average and maximum playbooks attached per case or alert, and identify playbooks with high rerun counts.
  • Execution latency diagnostics: Compare end-to-end playbook execution time against active action execution time, and drill down into the 30 slowest playbook and action runs.
  • Playbook and integration health monitoring: Investigate the latest failed playbook runs, highest failure-rate and terminated playbooks, and integration action error reasons.
  • Automation effectiveness metrics: Compare automated versus manual case closure rates and Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR).

For more information, see Monitor response and playbook health.

entry.content:

BigQuery

Feature

The BigQuery Data Engineering Agent is now available in the asia-northeast1 (Tokyo) regional endpoint and supports the gemini-3.5-flash model. For more information, see Where Gemini in BigQuery processes your data.

This feature is Generally Available (GA).

Cloud SQL for MySQL

Feature

Note: Near real-time sync upon Knowledge Catalog (KC) enablement isn't available for existing instances created before April 18, 2026. For more information, see the release note from October 14, 2026.

When you enable Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog) integration on an eligible Cloud SQL for MySQL instance created before April 18, 2026 where the integration is currently turned off, the instance now syncs schema and metadata updates to Knowledge Catalog in near real-time instead of once a day (instances created on or after April 18, 2026 have near real-time sync enabled by default).

This feature is available for instances running MySQL version 8.0 or later on the new network architecture. If Knowledge Catalog integration is already enabled on the instance with once-a-day updates, you can deactivate and re-enable the integration to switch to near real-time updates.

For more information, see Enable the integration of Knowledge Catalog on an existing Cloud SQL instance.

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL

Feature

Note: Near real-time sync upon Knowledge Catalog (KC) enablement isn't available for existing instances created before April 18, 2026. For more information, see the release note from October 14, 2026.

When you enable Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex Universal Catalog) integration on an eligible Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance created before April 18, 2026 where the integration is currently turned off, the instance now syncs schema and metadata updates to Knowledge Catalog in near real-time instead of once a day (instances created on or after April 18, 2026 have near real-time sync enabled by default).

This feature is available for instances running PostgreSQL version 14.0 or later on the new network architecture. If Knowledge Catalog integration is already enabled on the instance with once-a-day updates, you can deactivate and re-enable the integration to switch to near real-time updates.

For more information, see Enable the integration of Knowledge Catalog on an existing Cloud SQL instance.

For more information, see the following:

  • Map SQL Server data types to Datastream unified types
  • Data type mappings in BigQuery

Announcement

Sale of Gemini Code Assist subscriptions is ending. Starting October 9, 2026, new Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise subscriptions can no longer be purchased. Existing subscriptions will continue to auto-renew through the rest of 2026, but auto-renewal will end in 2027. For more information, see Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise subscriptions.

For alternative AI developer tools, use Antigravity, which is available through eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions and through Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

Announcement

Sale of Gemini Code Assist subscriptions is ending. Starting October 9, 2026, new Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise subscriptions can no longer be purchased. Change

Looker

Announcement

Beginning October 5, 2026, the following features will be automatically enabled for Looker (original) instances running Looker 26.18. Feature enablement for Looker (Google Cloud core) will be announced separately.

Feature

Looker now includes built-in support for the Dremio 26.0+ (Arrow Flight SQL) dialect. The Dremio 26.0+ (Arrow Flight SQL) uses the bundled Apache Arrow Flight SQL JDBC driver, so that you don't have to install unpackaged custom JDBC driver JAR files. See the Dremio documentation page for more information.

Feature

The AI-Assisted Quick Starts feature, called Starter questions in the new Explore experience, is now generally available.

Feature

The new Diagnose & Repair tool evaluates your LookML project repository across eight diagnostic test checks in either your personal development environment or the shared production environment. When issues are found, Looker can automatically perform repairs (such as removing stale lock files, fixing file permissions, or repairing corrupted object indexes) or rebuild damaged repositories while safeguarding uncommitted changes on a dedicated recovery branch.

Feature

Looker Continuous Integration (CI) now includes the Style Validator, which enforces LookML coding standards, naming conventions, and structural best practices across your LookML project. You can run the Style Validator with the default built-in ruleset or customize rule severities, file exclusions, path overrides, and custom rules by adding an lkmlstyle.yaml configuration file to your project repository.

Feature

Now available in preview, Conversational Analytics agentic workflows support scheduled agentic workflows in addition to triggered agentic workflows. You can use scheduled agentic workflows to schedule recurring deliveries of AI-generated insights summaries, data tables, visualizations, and PDF reports to email or Slack by using natural language. Recipients can select Investigate in a workflow notification to open a private, persistent conversation with the data agent.

Users and admins can manage workflows on the updated Manage Workflows user page and Manage Workflows admin page, respectively, and Looker admins can monitor scheduled workflow runs and troubleshoot errors on the new Workflow Executions admin page.

Workflows that were created in versions earlier than Looker 26.14 appear on the Legacy Workflows tab and must be recreated.

Feature

Now available in preview, Looker Data Apps are freeform canvas dashboards that are built by local AI coding agents, such as Gemini CLI, Claude Code, or Cursor, from natural-language prompts. Data Apps give you complete visual layout control (including absolute positioning, overlapping elements, and custom web components) while remaining bound to Looker's governed LookML semantic layer and user permissions.

Change

In Conversational Analytics, the default question mode is now Fast rather than Thinking. Fast mode is intended for answering quickly, and it directly maps your query to underlying LookML definitions without generating reasoning steps. You can still select Thinking mode from the question mode drop-down menu when asking complex, multi-step analytical questions about Explores or dashboards.

Change

The Modern User Interface preview feature toggle now defaults to ON.

Change

The Modern visualization theme now supports map charts (static map points and regions), word cloud charts, and donut multiples. While support for donut multiples was previously documented, it is now officially available with this release. These additions expand the range of visualization options that are available with the modern theme.

Feature

Looker now supports connections to the ClickHouse 26+ dialect. ClickHouse 26+ uses modernized JDBC drivers and introduces support for symmetric aggregates. See the ClickHouse documentation page for more information.

Model Armor

Feature

Model Armor includes enhanced prompt injection and jailbreak protection for Workspace data. This capability improves detection accuracy and minimizes false positives when screening Workspace content, such as emails, documents, and files.

This capability is available on multi-region endpoints in the US (us) and EU (eu) for templates and floor setting configured with filter version v3 or later, including the Stable and Latest aliases.

Secure Web Proxy

Feature

Secure Web Proxy supports global access. You can enable this feature when creating a Secure Web Proxy instance to make sure that clients from any Google Cloud region can connect to your proxy.

With global access, you can route your outbound traffic through specific regions to meet regulatory compliance or cost requirements. You can also use this option to simplify your network administration by managing outbound traffic from a centralized location.

This feature is available in Preview.

Security Command Center

Feature

Using gcloud CLI, the securitycenter REST API, or client libraries, you can configure Pub/Sub and BigQuery continuous export to receive notifications when findings are deleted from Security Command Center due to data retention policies.

For more information, see the following:

  • Enable finding notifications for Pub/Sub
  • Stream findings to BigQuery for analysis
  • Enable real-time notifications
  • Creating and managing Notification Configs

Sensitive Data Protection

Change

If you set InfoType.version to legacy when including the MEDICAL_ID infoType in your InspectConfig, Sensitive Data Protection now includes MEDICAL_RECORD_NUMBER findings as type MEDICAL_ID in the scan results.

entry.title: October 08, 2026
entry.content:
Cloud SQL for MySQL

Feature

Cloud SQL for MySQL now supports the innodb_cloudsql_managed_buffer_pool_tuneup_pct database flag.

Managed buffer pool automatically adjusts the InnoDB buffer pool size to reduce out-of-memory events. When instance memory usage remains at or below 70% for 10 minutes or longer after prior reductions, Cloud SQL increases the buffer pool size. You can now use the innodb_cloudsql_managed_buffer_pool_tuneup_pct flag to change this 70% threshold to a different percentage. Increase the threshold to restore the InnoDB buffer pool size when baseline usage exceeds 70%, or decrease it to preserve additional RAM allocation for memory spikes.

This flag requires the Cloud SQL maintenance version MYSQL_VERSION.R20260726.00_05 or later. For more information, see Enable managed buffer pool.

Feature

Cloud SQL for MySQL supports blue-green deployments (Preview).

Blue-green deployments let you update databases—such as performing major version upgrades from MySQL 8.0 to 8.4 and staging hardware or configuration modifications—while minimizing downtime. During a blue-green deployment, Cloud SQL creates a separate staging environment (green) that mirrors your existing production environment (blue) and maintains continuous logical replication from blue to green. You can test application compatibility and performance on the green environment without affecting production traffic, and then trigger a switchover to the green environment with minimal application downtime.

For more information, see About blue-green deployments in Cloud SQL.

Compute Engine

Feature

Generally available: You can sync a Compute Engine VM's clock with its host server's clock by using chrony and ptp_kvm to achieve accuracy designed to be within 1 ms. Accurate time synchronization is supported in all standard public Google Cloud regions and zones. For more information, see Configure accurate time for Compute Engine VMs.

Administrators can enable Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) and Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) for AI developer tools (Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity CLI, and Antigravity for IDEs). Third-party models are turned off by default:

  • In-console Terms of Service consent flow: Administrators can opt in to Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 directly in Gemini Enterprise > Settings > AI developer tools > Antigravity authorized models in the Google Cloud console without a separate Anthropic account or onboarding. For more information, see Configure AI developer tools settings.
  • Location availability: Third-party model inference is available in the global, us, and eu locations (in-country regions aren't supported). For a list of countries and regions that can access the model, see Anthropic's Supported countries and regions.
  • Consumption billing: Third-party model usage is billed as consumption on your Cloud Billing account and counts toward your project's spend cap, which covers all models. Overages must be turned on before you can enable a third-party model. For more information, see Configure overages and the Cloud Billing SKUs for Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5.
  • Thinking levels: Developers sign in with their existing Gemini Enterprise license and select Claude Opus 5.5 or Claude Sonnet 5.5 in the model picker at a thinking level of Low, Medium, High, or Max (for example, Claude Opus 5.5 (High)). Medium is the default.

Fixed

This release addresses the following issues:

  • Fixed an issue where agents could be assigned more concurrent chats than their configured maximum limit when multiple chat offers arrived almost simultaneously.

  • Fixed an issue where calls were unevenly distributed among available agents on skills-based queues.

  • Fixed an issue where supervisor-initiated sign-outs silently discarded mandatory interaction dispositions during an agent's wrap-up period.

  • Fixed an issue where an agent's corporate email address and internal ID were exposed in the browser's network metadata during a virtual agent to human escalation.

  • Fixed an issue where voice calls were incorrectly routed back to the virtual agent queue instead of the intended destination.

  • Fixed an issue where inbound callers experienced a 2-second delay when connecting to an agent.

Looker

Announcement

Looker 26.20 will roll out to Looker (original) and Looker (Google Cloud core) instances on the following schedule:

  • Expected deployment start: Monday, October 12, 2026
  • Expected final deployment and download available: Sunday, October 25, 2026

Looker 26.20 is expected to include the following changes, features, and fixes.

Breaking

Custom TopoJSON URL validation is updated to improve security. This change is isolated to Google Maps rendering in preview. Existing dashboards and Looks with the Google Maps Enhancements preview feature enabled that use custom TopoJSON files may be impacted.

Feature

The Gemini in Looker admin page has been restructured to allow Looker admins to selectively enable Conversational Analytics features and capabilities. Enablement for generally available Conversational Analytics features is now organized under the follow settings:

  • Conversational Analytics (Conversations page): Enables access to the Conversations page for data agents with Explores and direct chats with an Explore.
  • Dashboard agents: Enables default data agents on user-defined and LookML dashboards.
  • Additional options: Allows Conversational Analytics data agent creators to enable the Advanced Analytics feature for all conversations with their data agent. To use Advanced Analytics, you must also enable whichever Conversational Analytics toggle corresponds to the content that you are querying (Conversational Analytics (Conversations page) or Dashboard agents). If both the Conversational Analytics (Conversations page) and Dashboard agents toggles are turned off, then Advanced Analytics cannot be enabled. If either Conversational Analytics (Conversations page) or Dashboard agents is enabled, Advanced Analytics can be enabled, but it is turned off by default.

The Conversational Analytics (Conversations page) and Dashboard agents settings inherit the enablement state of the Conversational Analytics setting in previous versions of Looker.

Conversational Analytics preview features can still be enabled selectively under the Enable Trusted Tester Features setting.

(Note: This item was added on October 14, 2026.)

Feature

Conversational Analytics data agents for both user-defined dashboards and LookML dashboards are now generally available.

(Note: This item was added on October 14, 2026.)

Feature

You can now apply themes to Looks in addition to internal dashboards.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where duplicating a scheduled plan could fail to retain the custom message value. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

Table visualizations now proportionally scale left-pinned columns during automatic sizing, which prevents unnecessary horizontal scrollbars. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where enabling subtotals on table visualizations did not automatically disable the Cell Visualizations option. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where previews for Looker charts in Slack integrations could fail to be displayed. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where editing and saving a dashboard could cause the dashboard to reload indefinitely, forcing users to refresh the page. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where table cell visualizations that included both positive and negative values could display unwanted scrollbars and hide value labels. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where the BigQuery JDBC driver could fail to properly parse certain data types, such as BYTES, STRUCT/RECORD, and nested ARRAY structures. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where linked filters on a dashboard could fail to display autocomplete suggestions even when a parent filter is selected. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

The System Activity query_metrics Explore has been updated to ensure that phase timings (such as connection acquisitions, execution runtimes, and optimistic pivot fallback retry loops) are successfully captured for queries that fail or time out. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

The System Activity Dashboard Diagnostics dashboard has been updated to fully support statistics, tile run counts, and performance recommendations for LookML dashboards. This feature now performs as expected.

Fixed

An issue has been fixed where the color palette popover in visualization settings failed to dynamically reposition when it expanded, causing controls to overlap or truncate. This feature now performs as expected.

Breaking

When you set up a connection, self-service modeling will now be available only if a role that grants create_self_service_from_table also selects it through that role's model set.

Fixed

The opacity for the comparison bar in short KPI visualizations has been reduced to increase legibility.

Memorystore for Redis

Feature

To help protect your data and provide a baseline level of persistence, RDB snapshots are enabled by default when you create an instance using the Google Cloud console. This feature is generally available.

VPC Service Controls

Feature

General availability support for the following integration:

  • Cloud Storage for Firebase

Feature

VPC Service Controls feature (Status: Preview): Support for automated remediation suggestions is available in the VPC Service Controls violation analyzer.

Remediation suggestions analyze access denial events and generate actionable, narrowly scoped configuration changes to resolve perimeter denials and adhere to the principle of least privilege. The remediation engine can automatically propose ingress rules, egress rules, VPC accessible services updates, and existing or new context-aware access levels.

For more information, see Resolve access denials with remediation suggestions.

v1.14.9

On October 7, 2026 we released an updated version of the Apigee hybrid software, v1.14.9.

  • For information on upgrading, see Upgrading Apigee hybrid to version v1.14.9.
  • For information on new installations, see The big picture.
Note: This is a patch release: The container images used in patch releases are integrated with the Apigee hybrid Helm charts. Upgrading to a patch via the Helm chart automatically updates the images. No manual image changes are typically needed. For information on container image support in Apigee hybrid releases, see Apigee release process.

Fixed

Fixed in this release

Bug ID Description
565072374 Fixed an issue where VerifyJWT policies using a JWKS uriRef could return steps.jwt.NoMatchingPublicKey on the first request after the 5-minute JWKS cache TTL expired when the identity provider rotated keys. The cache now refreshes synchronously upon expiration.
564969400 Fixed an issue where variables initialized from an empty <Value/> element in AssignMessage (AssignVariable) were not treated as empty strings when referenced in message template functions such as replaceAll.
558888960 Fixed an issue in distributed tracing where the target URL was omitted from outbound target request span attributes after a request-flow policy step executed.
554114419 Apigee hybrid now allows policies to modify HTTP/2 request pseudo-headers (:path and :authority) when communicating over HTTP/2.
548763108 Hardened Message Processor outbound HTTP validation to block requests to internal Kubernetes cluster hostnames (*.svc.cluster.local).
513032450 Fixed an issue where apigee-connect-agent control-plane connections could hang for up to 2 hours when silently dropped by a network intermediary by restoring a 15-second TCP keep-alive.
